So, I’m a new player, i play on PC, and honestly, my first impression of Tower of Fantasy was pretty good! I customised my character and she turned out SO cute.💕 I was really happy with her, and the character customisation is definitely one of the things I liked the most. I’m still a little confused about the gacha system and how exactly you’re supposed to get weapons/characters, though. I’m usually more into classic MMORPGs, so I’m not really used to this kind of system. The game also throws a LOT of information at you at the beginning, and I’ll admit… I was too lazy to read all of it. 😭 So some of my confusion is probably partly my fault. I also ran into some issues with the voice acting/audio. Some voice lines seemed to be missing, while others were suddenly in English even though I had set my voice language to Japanese. It was pretty weird and took me out of the experience a little. But the biggest problem I had was the story progression. The game really doesn't feel very beginner-friendly if you're trying to actually follow the story in order. I got what felt like a massive spoiler very early on, because at some point the game suddenly wanted to send me to Vera or something??? And suddenly I was seeing Shirli's new appearance and getting information that, as a completely new player, I definitely wasn't expecting to see yet. At first, I genuinely thought my game had bugged out or that I had somehow skipped a bunch of quests. But then I checked my quests because I’m familiar with classic MMORPGs and I thought, "Okay, maybe I should check what I'm actually supposed to be doing before I follow this new quest." And that's when I realised that the story I was actually supposed to be experiencing had basically been pushed aside and turned into a side/Memory quest, while the game was trying to move me forward into later content. And honestly… WHAT 😭 I understand that the game is trying to help players catch up with the newer content, and technically the older story isn't gone. I could manually go back and track the original quests. But as a new player, I shouldn't have to already know that. If I'm playing the game for the first time and the game tells me to follow the main quest, I'm obviously going to assume that the main quest is the story I'm supposed to be following. Instead, I suddenly found myself being pushed into later content and seeing characters and story developments that I hadn't properly reached yet. That's what bothered me the most. I even looked online afterwards because I genuinely thought this was just something weird happening to my game, but I found other new players talking about having the exact same confusion. So I don't think Tower of Fantasy is necessarily a bad game. I actually think there's a lot here that I could enjoy. The graphics are really pretty, the character customisation is adorable, and I'm sure the game becomes much easier to understand once you've played it for a while. But I do think the onboarding is really confusing for a completely new player. There's a lot of information thrown at you, the gacha system can be confusing if you're coming from a more traditional MMORPG background, and the way the story progression works can make it really easy to accidentally spoil yourself or think you've skipped something. And for me personally, that really killed my motivation to continue. I didn't finish the game because I stopped playing after that. I did try to continue the original story manually, but honestly, I was still disappointed that I had already been shown such a major development before I was supposed to experience it. So, as someone who is new to Tower of Fantasy, I wouldn't personally recommend it as a first MMORPG if you're someone who really cares about following the story naturally and understanding everything as you go. That doesn't mean I think the game is bad. It's more like… I think Tower of Fantasy can be enjoyable once you understand how everything works, but getting to that point as a new player can be unnecessarily confusing. 😭 Still, the graphics are beautiful, and the character customisation is genuinely SO good. 💕 That's probably the part I had the most fun with!

Tower of Fantasy, developed by Hotta Studio and published by Perfect World Games, is an ambitious free-to-play open-world MMORPG that blends futuristic science fiction with anime-inspired visuals and large-scale online multiplayer gameplay. Set on the distant planet of Aida, the story revolves around humanity's attempt to escape Earth's decline and build a new civilization powered by the mysterious Omnium energy. What begins as a technological breakthrough soon leads to disaster, leaving the world scarred by catastrophe and filled with dangerous creatures, rival factions, and forgotten mysteries. This narrative creates an engaging backdrop for a massive adventure that emphasizes exploration, action, and social interaction. The game's greatest achievement is the sheer scale of its world. Aida is packed with varied environments that constantly reward curiosity, from dense forests and sandy deserts to towering futuristic cities and frozen mountain ranges. Every region is filled with hidden treasures, environmental puzzles, exploration challenges, and optional activities that encourage players to venture away from the main storyline. Traversal feels fluid thanks to climbing, gliding, jetpacks, vehicles, and other mobility tools that make crossing long distances enjoyable instead of tedious. The combination of natural beauty and advanced technology gives each location its own personality, making exploration one of the most satisfying aspects of the experience. Combat stands out by favoring speed and flexibility over traditional MMORPG mechanics. Instead of selecting a permanent character class, players equip multiple weapons that can be swapped instantly during combat. Each weapon possesses its own abilities, elemental attributes, and fighting style, allowing players to create personalized combinations suited for different encounters. Battles are fast-paced and visually exciting, with perfectly timed dodges triggering slow-motion opportunities that reward precision and quick reactions. Boss encounters demand careful positioning and coordination, while ordinary enemies rarely become repetitive because of the wide variety of weapon combinations available throughout the game. Character customization also receives considerable attention. Players begin by creating their own avatar using an extensive selection of appearance options, giving everyone the opportunity to build a unique identity within the online world. As progression continues, equipment upgrades, relics, weapon enhancements, and additional customization systems steadily expand combat possibilities. The game also introduces Simulacra, powerful weapon users whose personalities, stories, and visual designs add additional flavor to the world without limiting player freedom. This approach successfully balances player creativity with memorable characters that enrich the game's lore. The multiplayer component reinforces Tower of Fantasy's MMORPG identity. Players can join friends or strangers to complete cooperative dungeons, challenge enormous world bosses, participate in guild activities, and engage in competitive multiplayer modes. Shared exploration naturally encourages teamwork, as players often encounter one another while traveling through the world or responding to large-scale events. Seasonal updates, limited-time activities, and expanding regions help maintain long-term interest, ensuring that both new and veteran players regularly have fresh objectives to pursue. Visually, the game presents a colorful and highly stylized interpretation of science fiction. Anime-inspired character models, impressive visual effects, detailed environments, and futuristic architecture combine to create an appealing presentation that remains consistent throughout the adventure. The soundtrack complements each region effectively, shifting from peaceful orchestral themes during exploration to energetic compositions during combat. Smooth animations and flashy weapon skills further enhance the excitement of battles without sacrificing overall visual clarity. The narrative offers an interesting mix of science fiction, mystery, and survival. As players uncover the history of Omnium energy and the downfall of civilization on Aida, they gradually learn more about the world's factions, political struggles, and hidden secrets. While the storytelling occasionally progresses at an uneven pace, the setting itself remains compelling thanks to its rich lore and unique blend of futuristic technology and post-apocalyptic themes. The game succeeds in establishing an identity that differs from more traditional fantasy MMORPGs while providing enough world-building to encourage continued exploration. Like many modern free-to-play online games, Tower of Fantasy includes progression systems tied to premium currencies, collectible weapons, cosmetics, and ongoing live-service updates. Players can experience a substantial amount of content without making purchases, but acquiring specific premium weapons or maximizing endgame performance may require considerable time investment or optional spending. Those familiar with gacha mechanics will recognize these systems immediately, while others may find the monetization less appealing despite the generous amount of free content available. Overall, Tower of Fantasy successfully combines expansive open-world exploration, stylish real-time combat, deep customization, and large-scale multiplayer systems into a polished online adventure. Its impressive environments, satisfying weapon mechanics, and cooperative gameplay create a rewarding experience for players who enjoy persistent online worlds and continuous content updates. Although its live-service design and monetization may not appeal to everyone, the game delivers a rich science-fiction MMORPG filled with memorable locations, engaging action, and meaningful opportunities for exploration and teamwork. Rating: 7/10

*UPDATE* I still love this game *END OF UPDATE* I started playing this game around the start of April 2026. It is May 22nd, 2026 and I am 203.2 hours into it. I'm having an absolute blast and I've spent $0 on this game. I see this game has gotten some flak for a few things, so I thought I'd make a few points/counter points to things that have been said. I saw someone say "There's no real story or point to the game" I disagree with that. The story is pretty detailed on what's going on, and as you progress for area to area, you see how each area is being affected by what is going on in the story. Is it the best, most moving story ever? No, but I'd give it a 7/10 for story at least. I saw another person say "Resources to raise weapons are ridiculously scarce for the amount it costs" I strongly disagree with that. In fact, I have the total opposite issue. My weapons are so maxed out, I am currently waiting to hit level 100 to raise them any further. That same person said "They introduce activities that you can't even feasibly do at recommended combat score and levels. Examples? Bygone Phantasm floor 11. I had over 10k combat score MORE than that floor, still can't clear it." 10k CS (combat score) isn't very powerful at all. My gf started playing after me; she has 27hrs and has a CS of 30k. After 203hrs my CS is around 133k. Bygone Phantasm is also an endless fight to see how far you can get, not to beat. I have made it to floor 315, and have hit "the wall". The game is an MMO at the heart. You need closer to 30hrs (imo) to get an actual idea of it. Yes, it has it's issues. Some glitches, translation issues, quest lines trying to take you through walls, gacha-game mechanics everywhere, more than I can say here, but so does every MMO I've played, and I used to be an OG WoW player. I also can not attest to everything that happened when the switch from Tencent to PWG and the loss of accounts, as I joined post issues. Currently, the game is a blast, the community is helpful (on my server at least), and I'm probably going to put another 200hrs this year. P.S. I am not calling out anyone who's comments I referred to. I used them to justify my counterpoints.

I’ve played ToF for a long time, and enjoyed it for the character customization and open world. It was one of my favourite anime games, until they’ve removed the difficulty options in Joint Operations. That was the only gamemode where pets could fight alongside you, and now the JO enemies scale with your level, making them unfairly tanky. I have a lot of good memories from playing ToF, but it looks like the devs abandoned it at this point. The recent updates haven’t done anything to add game modes involving pets, or letting you explore the overworld with them. It’s been more than year since I’ve put those suggestions in a survey, and yet the pet system remains stagnant. It’s sad the devs have forgotten about this core feature. These shortcomings with ToF can’t help me but compare it to another online, open world game: No Man’s Sky. No Man’s Sky recently added the Xeno Arena update, which added a simulated pet combat mode (like Pokemon). Additionally, the amount of pets you could own was increased from 18 to 30. That update alone made NMS further surpass ToF, as NMS also had overworld pets for years instead of them being permanently in an enclosure on the Artificial Island. Unlike ToF, No Man’s Sky remembered and improved one of the biggest features in an open world game, being the vast roster of fantastical, alien creatures as companions. Tower of Fantasy is close to being a great game, but the devs’ neglect (and arguably even suppression) of a core feature made it a shadow of itself that’s just out of greatness’s reach. I’m doubtful that their new game, Neverness to Everness, will be successful either, as it will just be another set of wasted potential for Hotta to abandon. Even after having successfully transferred the account with my original progress, I don’t think I’ll return to this game for a while.

Theres a lot ive got to say aboout this game both good and bad, as of the current state of the game right now though, mostly bad. And its not even from a conceptual standpoint. Starting with the good things, this game is fairly easy and progression feels nice, satisfying and linear, the romance is nice and sweet and rewarding but theres also genuine times too where your relationship with a character actually feels like one. The open world aspect when it goes smoothly unaffected by bugs is really rewarding and super fun, im a sucker for a good open world game. But, unfortunately because of the absurd amount of bugs in this game and weird in game mechanics meant to hold your hand, said exploration as the game intends just becomes super annoying really fast and at times just becomes so tedious, which is a shame because this game for being free has so much open world content with many areas for you to wander around. The amount of bugs in this game both minor and some more major and game breaking is insane to me for a game that is iirc three years into release. For reference, the in game menu has an unstuck button just so you know what you could be getting into lol. If i went into extensive detail into all the bugs ive found a mere 50 hours into this game wed be here forever so im just going to rapid fire the ones most annoying to me off the top of my head. Bugs will freeze in place and not "run" from you, huntable animals often will freeze in place and eat your arrows and not take that damage and then teleport away randomly, NPCS are un-interactable at times and also teleport to other locations before you can actually talk to them, NPCS and item drops from resources or hunting sometimes do not appear and are invisible to you only popping up the collect or talk to icon, sometimes whilst travelling across the world for no explicable reason youll just teleport backwards and need to remake that distance all over again, animations for chopping trees and mining will sometimes play out almost all the way through then your character for no reason just stops and you have to replay the three second animation for your "damage" to actually register that time extending the time it takes to get resources by a lot if youre grinding, sometimes your character when spawning into a new location will be teleported instead to a white void where your stuck in a falling animation and have to use the in game unstuck button, your character also will sometimes spawn bald, ive seen other players just sliding around the map in like a T pose position before, sometimes ill see gates and doorways stuck open when they only are supposed to open and close when you get near/away from them, and lastly, when playing sometimes for no reason my view in game will just flick a random direction and mess up my aim or where im trying to go when travelling from place to place, a problem ive never had with any other game and its not a problem with my mouse i checked. I want to so badly reccomend this game because I can tell besides the bug aspect a lot of love went into the game and the characters and the routes and gameplay and world and story building but all these very mildly infuriating bugs make the way the game is intended to be played all the more mildly annoying when all of these happen often enough and one of these at least once everytime I pick up the game, that I just cant reccomend it fully in good faith. Another problem this game also suffers from is strange game mechanics and janky ass hitboxes that make the game regarding travel and so forth that little bit more unfun. Like mounts for example will catch on the hitbox of any little thing, a fence, a gate a tiny little bush or tree or a wall or rock and need to do a complete full stop for a second or two then on top of that play another like 2-3 second animation of it rearing up before you can actually move and start to get going again, which when youre travelling through dense forested areas and you end up hitting every tiny little bush just to travel to the other side of an area is SO incredibly infuriating so fast especially when this game has such detailed wild areas and such. At times just to skip all the bull, I just unmount and remount because its faster to do that then sit through all that time of animations playing. it also does not help, and perhaps this is an issue with my mount seeing as I just have the tutorial one they give you but the turn radius on the horses are so incredibly stiff that it makes it that much harder to avoid every little stone. I get trees having hitboxes and stuff but when things like a tiny little shrub or a single pile of rocks or hell even a tiny little unsmooth incline makes me fullstop every time it makes me so annoyed that id literally just rather walk if the areas youre meant to explore and travel werent so large. I should not feel this about a game that has its story deeply rooted in its open worldness but the game at times honestly feels like its fighting you when you try to go anywhere with the resources they give you. The fact as well that you can "drown" in waist deep water is so incredibly annoying especially when it happens so fast that it ruins the flow of traversing the map when I walk through maybe a river too deep or a pond in the way and I immediately get teleported backwards sometimes a really far distance as it teleports you where you last touched safe land, for water that was hardly deep at all again in a game where the world around is so detailed and filled with lots of rivers and water features. It just ruins my emersion of the game and instead now im sitting there questioning why the game is made this way as I need to move around the entire damn thing to keep moving forward. Another thing i also forgot to mention intiially is how quests will auto-pin themself which makes you need to open the quest menu and.unpin.them.indivisually.every.single.time. But yeah, its just in general, this game suffers a lot more from downsides than it does upsides which is a real shame because this game is something I genuinely could see myself sinking hours and hours into because of how engaging other aspects of the game are but I just cannot get over how buggy the base game is and how sometimes Ill be doing something super fun then Ill get reminded how this game unfortunatley is flawed and in a very broken state just by playing the game the way it was intended. For all the fun you can get out of the game theres 20 bugs that you encounter so again, i really just cant in fully goo faith reccomend this game to anyone. Theres other games on the market open world and better coded and structured than this one....

I cannot in good faith recommend Palia to anyone like me. The game looks nice, the premise is interesting and I love the characters so far. However, that's as far as I can go with the positives. Don't get me wrong; I love this game so far... but it's just unhealthy for me to continue playing. Palia is buggy, extremely so. I would understand if it was made by a small indie team or if it was a more recent game, but it isn't - Palia has been out for three years now. I'm someone who doesn't try to encounter bugs, but I have faced several in my hours playing. You can get sent flying up into the sky from playing a minigame, you will clip into objects, animals you are hunting will suddenly teleport away or run under the water where you can't reach them. People say Palia is still in beta, but that's no excuse for this behavior lasting this long. Pay elements are everywhere, and I mean everywhere. You cannot exist in Palia without finding an in-game ad asking you to fork over your money for subscriptions and cosmetics and the ability to get around much faster with a horse. All a free player gets in terms of character customization are some hairs and basic clothing, but if you want to customize beyond that, you HAVE to pay real money. There's no other way to customize besides paying up, or you'll look bland and boring forever. I think the game specifically knows this, because the cosmetics offered in the premium shop are things anyone would enjoy, especially cottagecore folks like myself. I <3 (character) shirts, meme clothing, dresses, emotes, pets, ect. There is not a single quest in the game, from my research, that gifts for clothes or lets you craft it yourself. It's not like the cosmetics are cheap, either! Some sets are worth nearly $50 USD. There's even a battle pass. So, yeah, while there's memes and Jimothy plushes, this game is extremely predatory. The devs don't care how broken it all is or how your experience goes, they just want money.
